title: Watching a Thanksgiving Parade
description: Watch a holiday parade through familiar performers, decorations, and places beside the route.
cardDescription: Watch a holiday parade through familiar performers, decorations, and places beside the route.
focus: The clues describe things seen or heard during a parade. Some answers name objects, while others name a movement or a spectator action.
solvingTip: Look for a performer, a large decoration, a route feature, or a crowd action.
words: Organized procession held for a holiday celebration
Decorated platform moving through a parade
Inflated display object carried or guided in a parade
Short stick carried by a parade leader or twirler
Percussion instrument providing a marching beat
Large low brass instrument heard in a marching band
To walk in a regular organized procession
Planned path followed by a holiday parade
Long sign carried or displayed in a procession
Large gathering of spectators beside a parade route
Raised edge between a sidewalk and a street
To move a hand in greeting toward passing marchers
To call out approval during a parade

answerNotes.FLOAT: Float names a moving decorated platform here. It is not the act of remaining on water.
answerNotes.BATON: A parade baton is a carried or twirled stick. The same word also appears in conducting and relay running.
answerNotes.ROUTE: The route is the planned path. It names the course followed rather than the procession itself.
answerNotes.BANNER: A banner is a long display sign. It differs from an inflated decoration such as a balloon.

title: Family Around the Table
description: Gather familiar family names and host-and-guest words for a Thanksgiving visit.
cardDescription: Gather familiar family names and host-and-guest words for a Thanksgiving visit.
focus: The clues describe relationships rather than individual names. Several answers are familiar shortened family terms.
solvingTip: Look for a relationship, a generation, or a role at the gathering.
words: People connected through close kinship or household relationships
Child of one’s aunt or uncle
Sister of a parent, or a related family role by marriage
Brother of a parent, or a related family role by marriage
Familiar shortened name for a grandmother
Familiar shortened name for a grandfather
Person connected through a family relationship
Person invited to share a holiday meal
Person welcoming others to a Thanksgiving gathering

answerNotes.SIBLING: Sibling is a word covering a brother or sister. It identifies the relationship without naming one gender.
answerNotes.NIECE: A niece is a sibling’s daughter. A nephew is a sibling’s son, so the relationship words differ.
answerNotes.GRANDMA: Grandma is an informal form of grandmother. The clue asks for the familiar shortened word.
answerNotes.HOST: Host names the welcoming role here. It does not mean that every person at the table has the same family relationship.

title: Helpers in the Holiday Kitchen
description: Identify familiar kitchen helpers used around a large meal through their shapes and purposes.
cardDescription: Identify familiar kitchen helpers used around a large meal through their shapes and purposes.
focus: The clues name utensils and equipment rather than cooking steps. Some items hold food, while others move, separate, or support it.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue describes a container, a gripping tool, or a support.
words: Protective garment worn over clothes in a kitchen
Deep-bowled utensil used to serve soup or gravy
Paired gripping tool used to lift food
Perforated bowl used to drain food
Deep cooking pan associated with a large roast
Bulb-ended tube used to draw up and release cooking liquid
Heat-resistant support placed beneath a hot dish
Padded hand covering used for handling hot cookware
Raised framework supporting food or a pan
Rounded utensil used to stir or serve food
Pronged utensil used to lift or hold a portion
Edged kitchen tool used to cut food

answerNotes.COLANDER: A colander drains through holes. It is a complete bowl-shaped utensil rather than a single mesh insert.
answerNotes.BASTER: A baster draws liquid into a tube using a bulb. The clue identifies the object rather than a recipe instruction.
answerNotes.TRIVET: A trivet supports a hot dish. It is separate from the cookware placed on top of it.
answerNotes.TONGS: Tongs is a plural-form name for a paired gripping tool. The two arms work together as one implement.

title: Serving the Thanksgiving Pie
description: Explore pie service through familiar portions, fillings, nuts, and things placed on the table.
cardDescription: Explore pie service through familiar portions, fillings, nuts, and things placed on the table.
focus: The clues focus on the finished dessert and serving it. Shape and purpose help distinguish a portion, a topping, and a utensil.
solvingTip: Look for a food part, a serving shape, or an object used at the table.
words: Flat utensil used to lift a slice of pie
One cut serving from a pie
Pointed shape of a typical pie serving
Baked pastry around a pie’s filling
Mixture enclosed or supported by a pie crust
Rich dairy topping served with some desserts
Small rounded helping placed on a dessert
Nut used in a familiar Southern-style Thanksgiving pie
Wrinkled kernel used in some dessert fillings
Orchard fruit used in a classic holiday pie
Squash made into a familiar spiced holiday filling
Individual dish holding a served pie portion
Eating utensil used for a piece of pie
Container in which a pie is baked or served

answerNotes.DOLLOP: A dollop is a small rounded helping. The word does not specify a fixed measured quantity.
answerNotes.SERVER: Server is a serving utensil here. The same word can name a person bringing food to a table.
answerNotes.FILLING: Filling is a noun for the mixture inside the crust. It is different from the adjective describing a satisfying meal.
answerNotes.PECAN: Pecan names the nut used in the pie. Its name has several familiar regional pronunciations.

title: A Note of Thanks
description: Explore gratitude through familiar words for helping, sharing, gathering, and writing a short message.
cardDescription: Explore gratitude through familiar words for helping, sharing, gathering, and writing a short message.
focus: The clues describe ordinary gestures and relationships. A few common words have a specific meaning in a thank-you note.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a feeling, an action, a person, or a message.
words: Expression offered to acknowledge someone’s help
Feeling of appreciation for kindness received
Friendly and considerate treatment of others
To let others have a portion of something
To offer something to another person
Thoughtful attention to another person’s needs
Person known with affection and trust
Hope expressed for someone else’s happiness
To come together for a shared occasion

answerNotes.THANKS: Thanks is a plural-form expression of gratitude. Thank is the related verb used for the action.
answerNotes.NOTE: Note means a short written message here. It does not mean one musical pitch.
answerNotes.GATHER: Gather means come together in this clue. The same verb can describe collecting separate objects.
answerNotes.SHARE: Share is a verb about giving a portion here. It does not name a unit of company ownership.
